newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on DSM Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on DSM Q1 results.

text.p: Dutch petrochemicals group DSM NV said on Tuesday net profit for the first quarter of 1997 rose some nine percent to 223 million guilders from 205 million in the same period of 1996.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments:

"They are more or less in line with expectations but I would have liked the company to be more positive about the future. There were fears over chemical prices for the end of 1997 and they have gone away. Petrochemical companies in the U.S. are becoming more positive and I would have liked to see DSM follow.
But polymer prices are on the way up and DSM is on course for a very strong second quarter. We maintain it as a Buy."

"Better than expected and also the outlook was good but DSM is a little reluctant on its prospects. The decline in the naptha price will be a positive element this year. Underlying trend is positive and there is good volume growth. We had the stock as an outperformer and it will certainly remain so. I may even raise my estimates but I want to see more details first."

"Operating profit was right in line with our forecast. The only positive surprise was non-consolidated holdings where we had expected quite a sharp fall but in fact it stabilised...The forecast of a higher profit for the first-half is nice... We had been forecasting a five percent rise for the first half but that might be a bit conservative given DSM's statement...Our estimate of full-year EPS was 25.00 guilders, but I might have to raise that a little...As far as ratings are concerned, I don't think DSM is the most attractive chemical company, so I'm keeping it as an underperformer."
